# MVP Features — Orchard Core CMS on ServiceNow

> **Purpose.** Define the **smallest set of features** that delivers a usable, demonstrable CMS. Derived from `specs/DESIGN.md`, `specs/PLAN.md`, `specs/TASKS.md`, and `specs/design/coverage-matrix.md` (all 281 stories dispositioned).
>
> **MVP thesis.** A CMS earns its name the moment a user can: **define a content type → author a content item → move it through the publish lifecycle → have it rendered for an anonymous public visitor to browse**, all gated by roles and permissions. A headless REST API is also delivered for integrators. Everything that does not serve that thread is deferred.
>
> **Scope correction (public delivery).** `inputs/architecture.md` lists *"anonymous Site Visitors accessing published content"* as a first-class actor. The `specs/` translation went **headless** (REST + admin UI only) and omitted a public rendering layer. Per explicit product requirement, the MVP now **includes a public content delivery layer** so a visitor can browse a published page. This is net-new ServiceNow work not covered by the original 281-story disposition — see **Decision D6** and features **M23–M27**.
>
> **Scoping method.** We keep the whole "Build" content domain on the critical path, configure only the identity primitives the thread requires, and defer every multi-tenant / extensibility / secondary-integration story. Scope: `x_1863391_cms_cng`. Phase-0 decisions D1–D5 apply (single logical tenant, `content_item_version` child table, content types as data, GraphQL/XML-RPC deferred, thin query table).

---

## 1. The MVP critical path (end-to-end thread)

```text
  ┌─────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────┐     ┌───────────────────────┐
  │ Roles + ACLs        │ ──▶ │ Content Type + Fields │ ──▶ │ Author Content Item   │
  │ (who can do what)   │     │ (the shape)           │     │ (draft + versions)    │
  └─────────────────────┘     └──────────────────────┘     └───────────┬───────────┘
                                                                        │
                                                                        ▼
                                                          ┌───────────────────────────┐
                                                          │ Lifecycle                 │
                                                          │ Draft ▶ Published ▶ Removed│
                                                          └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                                                                        │
                        ┌───────────────────────────────┬──────────────┴───────────────┐
                        ▼                                ▼                               ▼
          ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────────┐
          │ Authoring UI             │    │ Content REST API          │    │ Public delivery            │
          │ (list + editor)          │    │ (retrieve / create)       │    │ (anonymous visitor browses │
          │                          │    │                           │    │  published page)           │
          └──────────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────┘    └────────────────────────────┘
```

If any box is missing, the product is not a CMS. That thread — **author → publish → public visitor browses it** — **is** the MVP.

---

### 2.7 Public content delivery (anonymous site visitors) — *net-new scope, see D6*
Enables the actual "publish a page and let the public browse it" outcome. Not in the original `specs/` disposition.

| # | Feature | Owning task (new) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| M23 | **URL slug** on content item (+ uniqueness among published items) | P2-03 extension | Data model (`ENT-04`) has no slug/route field; add `slug` (and auto-generate from title) so pages have friendly, stable URLs |
| M24 | **Anonymous read access** to published content only | P2-09 extension | Read ACL on `content_item` granting role `public` **only when `isPublished = true` and `state = Published`**; drafts/removed never exposed. Public read of the item's attachments (featured image) |
| M25 | **Public content delivery page(s)** — a published-content **index/list** + a **detail page** by slug, accessible to anonymous users | **P7-01 (new)** | Recommended: public **UI Page**(s) in-scope, server-side fetch of the published version, rendered with Horizon tokens; alternative = Service Portal. See D6 |
| M26 | **Field renderer + HTML sanitization** | **P7-02 (new)** | Map content-type fields (title, body/markdown, `customHtml`, featured image, publication date, tags) to safe markup; **sanitize `customHtml`/rich text** to prevent stored XSS on the public page |
| M27 | **Public-page accessibility + diagnostics** | **P7-03 (new)** | `ui_diagnostics` + WCAG 2.1 AA on the public pages (semantic landmarks, headings, alt text, contrast), light/dark + responsive |

## 4. DEFERRED — explicitly OUT of MVP

Grounded in coverage-matrix dispositions (D = Defer, plus secondary Build/Configure stories not on the critical thread).

| Area | Stories / tasks | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Multi-tenancy** (`tenant` table, provisioning, isolation) | EPIC-01, EPIC-16, P2-06, US-40a-04 | MVP runs single logical tenant (D1); tenancy adds cross-cutting ACL/data work |
| **Feature toggles** (`feature` table) | EPIC-07, P2-07 | Extensibility config, not core authoring |
| **Named queries** (`query` table + exec) | EPIC-09, EPIC-41 query stories, P2-08 | Content is browsable via list filters at MVP (D5 is thin but still non-core) |
| **Version pruning** scheduled job | P3-06, EPIC-42 retention | Retention housekeeping; not needed until version volume grows |
| **AI Search** indexing | EPIC-23/24/41, P4-06 | OOTB list search/filters cover MVP discovery; AI Search is an enhancement |
| **Notifications (email/SMS)** | EPIC-21/22/39, P4-08 | Tied to registration/verification, which is itself deferred (S5) |
| **GraphQL** API | EPIC-28, US-12b-01/02, P4-10 | Deferred by decision D4; REST satisfies MVP |
| **MetaWeblog / XML-RPC** | EPIC-30, US-12b-03, P4-11 | Lowest-value/highest-effort integration (D4) |
| **Deployment plans / remote deployment** | EPIC-08/17 deploy, EPIC-29, P4-14 | Replaced by Now SDK / Update Sets / App Repo; admin UX deferred |
| **Background processing / workflow automation** (polling, distributed locks, task gating) | EPIC-10/11, P4-09 | No MVP feature depends on it beyond lifecycle flows already in M10–M12 |
| **S3 / Azure Blob config screens** | EPIC-06/25/26 | Media remapped to Attachments (S2); external-storage config unneeded |
| **Advanced NFRs** (security headers, rate limiting, PII tuning, perf targets, DR docs) | EPIC-43/44, P6-02..06 | Rely on platform defaults for MVP; harden post-MVP |
| **SSO / OIDC / 2FA** | EPIC-20, US-37a-02/03, P1-10 | Local login (M2) is enough to demo and operate |

Already **covered by the platform** (never in scope as custom work): user/role data (OOTB `sys_user`/roles), schema migrations (Now SDK), persistence/cache/HA (platform DB/session/infra), CI harness (ATF).

---

## 5. MVP Definition of Done

1. An admin can create a **content type** with **fields** (M6–M7, M19).
2. An author can create and save a **draft content item**, producing versions (M8–M9, M13, M20).
3. The item can be **published, unpublished, cloned, removed, restored, and discarded**, with flags correct and validation enforced (M10–M14, M18).
4. The item is **retrievable and creatable via REST**, with the exact contracts/error codes in `inputs/api.md`, gated by roles/ACLs (M4, M15–M17).
5. A **published item is browsable by an anonymous visitor** at its slug URL — rendered, themed, accessible — while **drafts and removed items return not-found/forbidden** to the public (M23–M27).
6. All of the above is **permission-gated** and the **last-admin guard** holds (M1–M5).
7. Core thread passes **ATF**, and the custom editor **and public pages** pass **accessibility + `ui_diagnostics`** (M21–M22, M27).

When items 1–7 are green, the MVP is shippable.

---

## 6. New decision to ratify — D6 (public delivery mechanism)

Adding public browsing requires one architectural choice before building Phase 7.

| Option | Pros | Cons | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public UI Page(s)** in app scope (server-side fetch + render) | Lightweight; fully Fluent/Now SDK-defined in-scope; simplest anonymous access; least new metadata | Theming/a11y are hand-rolled; routing is `*.do`-style unless a processor is added for clean paths | **Recommended for MVP** — smallest correct footprint |
| **Service Portal** (portal + page + widget) | Purpose-built for public, themed, friendly-URL delivery; accessible defaults | Heavier; more metadata; portal theming overhead for a single page type | Choose if a richer public site is imminent |
| Next Experience / UI Builder public experience | Consistent with admin stack (Horizon, react-components) | Anonymous access is more involved; heavier for a read-only page | Not recommended for MVP |

### Public-delivery risks to control (all mechanisms)
- **Stored XSS:** `customHtml` and rich-text fields allow arbitrary HTML (`ENT-04.customHtml`). The public renderer **must sanitize/allowlist** (M26) — this is ship-blocking, not optional.
- **Over-exposure:** the anonymous ACL (M24) must filter on `isPublished = true` **and** `state = Published`; verify drafts/removed/other-version rows are never reachable, including via the featured-image attachment.
- **Public page registration:** the delivery page must be explicitly flagged public and must not widen anonymous access to any other table.
- **Slug collisions/stability:** enforce unique slugs among published items; decide behavior on retitle (keep stable slug).

> **Note:** `specs/` (DESIGN/PLAN/TASKS, coverage-matrix) still describe a headless build. If you approve this scope, those should gain a **Phase 7 — Public Content Delivery** and D6 so the specs and this MVP stay consistent. Say the word and I'll propagate it.
